req.title: Login form GET
req.statement: The system shall serve a login form at GET /auth/login.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /auth/login must return an HTTP 2xx response with a login form payload. I design: (1) a positive EP test verifying exact status 200 and presence of key HTML form elements (catches status-code mutations and content mutations); (2) a negative NEG test verifying that a wrong HTTP method (POST with no data) does NOT return 200 for the form-serving path — actually POST is allowed by the route, so I use a truly unsupported method (PUT) to get 405, confirming the route is method-guarded; (3) a BVA boundary test verifying the response Content-Type header contains 'text/html' and that the response body contains both 'username' and 'password' input fields, catching mutations that strip form fields; (4) a DT test verifying the exact byte-level presence of the HTML form action attribute pointing to /auth/login, catching mutations that alter the form target; (5) a STC test verifying that an already-logged-in user who GETs /auth/login still receives 200 (the login view does not redirect authenticated users away), confirming state-independence of the GET handler.

expected: Response body contains the HTML login form

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_login_get_returns_200_with_form():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/auth/login')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'username' in r.data
    assert b'password' in r.data
    assert b'<form' in r.data

test_login_get_returns_200_with_form()

tests.name: test_login_get_while_authenticated_still_returns_200
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temporary database
A user (Rahul, password=stone) exists in the database
The test client has an active session (user is logged in)
actions: POST to /auth/login with valid credentials to establish session
Follow redirect to confirm login succeeded
Send GET request to /auth/login while authenticated
expected: GET /auth/login returns exactly 200 even when a session exists
Response body still contains the login form elements
trace: R-FLASKR-007: the login view does not redirect authenticated users; GET always serves the form
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_login_get_while_authenticated_still_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login',
        data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/auth/login')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'name="username"' in r.data
    assert b'name="password"' in r.data

test_login_get_while_authenticated_still_returns_200()
